en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Thirteenth Chapter
The Discourse on Being Covered:
One who is covered abandons the hindrances? Yes.
"One who is lustful abandons lust; one who is hateful abandons hatred; one who is deluded abandons delusion; one who is defiled abandons defilements"?

One should not say this... [and so on] ... "One abandons lust by means of lust; one abandons hatred by means of hatred; one abandons delusion by means of delusion; one abandons defilements by means of defilements"?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is lust associated with consciousness? Is the path associated with consciousness? Yes.
Is there a convergence of two contacts …pe… of two consciousnesses?
One should not say so …pe…
Lust is unwholesome; the Path is wholesome.
(Agreed.
Do wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterparts, come into manifestation simultaneously?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Do wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterparts, come into manifestation? Yes.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Bhikkhus, there are these four things that are extremely remote. Which four?”
"The sky and the earth, monks—this is the first pair that is very far apart...
Therefore, the Dhamma of the virtuous is far from the wicked.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes.
In that case, it should not be said:
“Wholesome and unwholesome [states] …” etc.
“Do they come into manifestation? “Yes.
“Does one who is shrouded abandon the hindrances?
“Yes.”
But was it not said by the Blessed One:

"When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, stainless, free from defilements, become supple, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs his mind toward the knowledge of the destruction of the taints"?
Is there such a sutta?
“Yes,” he said.
“In that case, it should not be said:
‘One who is obstructed abandons the hindrances’ … [and so on] …”
Is it not to be said that one who is obstructed abandons the hindrances?
Yes, it is.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“For one who knows thus and sees thus, the mind is liberated even from the taint of sensual desire … [and so on] … the mind is liberated even from the taint of ignorance”?
Is that indeed the Sutta? Yes.
Then, by that very fact, one who is shrouded abandons the hindrances.
The Discourse on the Secluded is finished.
